Safe habits for farewell routines
This part of the manual describes how the desk handles it
Companion Animal Travel Desk farewell routine policy

Purpose: keep every pet calm, every traveler informed, and every handoff smooth from booking through pickup.

We keep the desk steady by checking documents, carrier condition, and routing notes before any animal moves toward the gate. Staff speak in short plain language, watch for stress, and keep the area clean so the next family does not inherit a mess. The shift lead stays close during handoffs and makes sure baggage, tags, and cabin notes line up before release.

For Port Isolde arrivals, <<FACT F027>> and the team uses that space only for animals cleared for quarantine care. Do not promise a kennel or move a pet into holding until the veterinary note is checked and the travel file is current. The pet lounge is used for brief comfort stops, slow water breaks, and calm waiting, but only when the desk has cleared the animal for that area. <<FACT F021>> and no one should send a traveler there before the desk confirms the pet is ready.

If a traveler brings a pet like Peanut, stay polite, keep the leash or carrier secure, and explain the next step without extra talk. When Lucia Rivera or Gabriel Rivera comes through with an animal, the same rule applies: verify the papers, repeat the handoff plan, and keep the path clear. Any sign of distress, escape risk, injury, or missing paperwork goes straight to the shift lead at once. Never improvise with medication, feeding, or release decisions, and never leave an animal unattended near doors or carts.

If the line backs up, separate waiting pets from moving traffic, reset the queue, and call for backup before the next handoff. Keep notes readable, keep the tone even, and keep the traveler from having to guess what happens next.

If anything looks off, contact the shift lead or the duty supervisor right away.
